thread: Compassion follows the line of sight: we answer the pain we are shown and arrange not to see the rest
summary: Each piece asks how much of our kindness depends on what happens to be in front of us, and what we do to stay out of the kitchen. Mencius argues it: a king spares an ox he can see and goes on eating the sheep he cannot, and the philosopher tells him that this is not a lack of ability but a refusal to use his sight. Auden images it: in the old paintings, a boy falls out of the sky and the ploughman and the ship go on with their day. Tolstoy dramatises it: a young man sees a kind officer do something terrible at dawn, says nothing, and quietly lets his own life shrink to avoid knowing what he knows. Vega sings around it: the speaker answers politely and asks for nothing, and the song's pressure falls on whoever is on the other side of the wall.

pieces.essay: Mencius argues it: pity is real but selective, and the gentleman who keeps away from the slaughter-house has mistaken a refusal to look for a virtue.
pieces.poem: Auden images it: the suffering is in the corner of the picture, and the world in the middle of the picture carries on.
pieces.story: Tolstoy dramatises it: the narrator sees, feels it, and withdraws without acting, then calls the whole thing chance.
pieces.song: Vega sings around it: the child answers the questions that would excuse the adults, and the listeners are left to decide what they heard.

forYou: In When Jasmine Blooms, the 1950s Malayan household and its servants can ask who in the house sees the violence, who arranges to be in another room, and who pays for that.
